items.line: Fabrizio Romano, a football transfer reporter, posts words he attributes to Mauricio Pochettino about taking the Manchester United job despite a new deal until 2030: "You can't turn it down". Not checked here.
Author Stephen King posts a joke that the real reason for the FAA ground stop is that aliens have landed and officials do not want a panic. It is a joke, not a report.

Jake Lucky, a streaming commentator, posts that IShowSpeed won Streamer of the Year at the Streamer Awards and gave his acceptance speech entirely in Indonesian. A reply from Overtime says the same of the speech.

Sky Sports Premier League reports that Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected a second contract offer from the club, with his deal due to expire at the end of the season. Not checked here.
Elon Musk posts "Starship 42 preparing for launch" with a link. He quotes another post. Not checked here.

Microsoft says it is deeply sorry for the outage and that service is broadly recovering. It says the cause was a network capacity upgrade followed by a network change, not a cyberattack or AI agents, and that it will publish a full post-incident report. Not checked here.

BRICS News, an aggregator account, says Russia reports that the first patient treated with a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine shows no signs of new tumors four months after treatment. Not checked here.
Valuetainment, a media account, says 88% of Nvidia employees voted for Jensen Huang to stay as CEO. Not checked here.

Shams Charania of ESPN reports that New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade, and that his agent and team officials have started working on a resolution. He cites sources. Not checked here.

BBC Breaking reports a rescue operation after a cargo ship collided with a cruise ship in New Orleans. Outlets including ABC and CBS describe a tanker striking a docked river cruise ship; the cause is not known. See the story on this site.
Fox News reports that the FAA has ordered all departing flights in the US to stay on the ground, and says this has happened only once before since 9/11. The post gives no cause. Not checked here.
Drone Wars, an account covering drone warfare, posts a video and says Ukrainian company ARMOLAB tested its ROBONOSH ground robotic evacuation system. Not checked here.
SpaceX posts a link to watch Starship Flight 15.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all US airports after a communication issue affecting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers, and that FAA technicians are investigating.
The White House account posts: "English is the official language of the United States."
An account named robotaxi says select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use. Not checked here.

The FAA's news account says there has been a temporary telecommunications outage, that all flights have been halted out of an abundance of caution, and that every flight is accounted for. The post does not say what caused the outage.

Gavin Newsom says President Trump was "MIA" while 1.5 million Americans were stranded at airports at a scale not seen since 9/11, and says Trump does not care about them. The figure and the comparison are his claims. Not checked here.

DiscussingFilm, a film news account, says Robert Pattinson was offered more money but only a three-film commitment for his audition deal to play James Bond, compared with the other finalists. It cites a source it does not name in the text. Not checked here.

Acyn, who posts clips of political events, shares a 35-second video in which a questioner asks whether something "could be AI related" and Mullin answers "We call it SI around here." The post does not say what the question is about. Not checked here.
WDSU, a New Orleans TV station, posts a video it credits to Kern Studios and says shows the moment a tanker struck a cruise ship in New Orleans. It says rescues are underway. Not checked here.

The fan account Avengers Updates posts a video it says is a new Disney+ teaser for "Avengers: Doomsday", with new dialogue from Doctor Doom: "Now you must answer to me. For I am Doom." Not checked here.

MKBHD, a tech reviewer, revisits his bet that Cybercab would be publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026. He says there are no deliveries yet, it is invite only and private use only. He tags Grok, which is made by xAI, the company behind the grabber. Not checked here.

Pope Leo XIV posts that transhumanism promises to end disease, pain and death, that scientific progress should not become a privilege of millionaires seeking immortality, and that in Christian teaching a limitation is not a manufacturing defect. He is on an apostolic journey to Peru, per his hashtags.

Balaji says two investment firms, Altimeter and Atreides, hold more than $25B in assets together, and that Elon Musk and the founders of Uber, Shopify, Replit and Vercel have posted support for reinstating Jensen Huang at Nvidia. He says board members opposed will face growing pressure. Not checked here.
The account yarslav posts a set of 20 images under the caption "20 years of YouTube in 1 tweet". Another account quotes it to say the site got worse at one point in that time.
The account GuGi263 posts a video it describes as an animal lover helping a cat whose tail was caught in metro doors. Not checked here.
JennieSTaer posts a video and says stuck travelers got a concert from the singer of Hoobastank during the nationwide air traffic shutdown. Not checked here.
PopBase, a pop culture account, says the tracklist for "GTA VI: The Album" has leaked online. Not checked here.
